top.line: SG/Send became sgit, and the record reordered my memory
top.para: SG/Send began as secure file sending with a server that holds nothing, and eight months later became sgit. Checking my memory against 4,476 app commits showed the vault was named before the features, a feature shipped in 22 minutes, and Git's model took two weeks. By 5 March the use case was missing.

in-short.line: Live in five days; the market said not yet
in-short.para: Client-side encryption, a first commit on 8 February and live on 13 February; Stripe on 1 March, ten paying customers on 2 March, folders as zips that evening. The vault and data room were named in February, sgit by 16 March, vault apps by May. Commits came on 246 of 249 days, but users did not return.

start.line: The best protection is never holding the asset
start.para: SG/Send solved a weekly problem: sending files securely without either side installing anything. It was the first product I shaped from the start with my security background. The first commit, on 8 February 2026, came with a spec: files encrypted on the client, key never sent, eliminating about 90% of the security risk surface.

live.line: send.sgraph.ai went live five days after commit one
live.para: A working zero-knowledge MVP on AWS Lambda was recorded on 12 February, and send.sgraph.ai went live on 13 February. The way of working was set the same day: voice memos become briefs, debriefs flow up. Explorers and villagers existed by 14 February, and the method produced 3,025 markdown files this year.

users.line: Ten paying customers, and a folder feature in minutes
users.para: A pricing brief of 28 February set £5 for 500 credits; Stripe went live on 1 March, and on 2 March there were ten paying customers, offered a £5 Amazon voucher. That evening a folder request went from proposal at 20:26 to code at 20:48 and a zip viewer at 22:15.

data-room.line: I had named the data room and vault first
data-room.para: On 3 March, emailing investors, I realised folder upload, the zip viewer and previews together were a data room, and the vault would be its editable evolution. The record shows I had named the data room between 17 and 21 February and a personal data vault on 22 February. The ideas came first.

git.line: Stop inventing: copy Git, with encryption on top
git.para: The 4 March brief said Git already solved versioning, so copy it: a dumb blob store server, intelligence in the client. It took about two weeks and 48 briefs, including a simulation that found 14 gaps and resolved 13. Deterministic encrypted ids made it work; sgit arrived 16 March, sgit-ai on PyPI 20 March.

vault.line: The vault grew from previews into sandboxed apps
vault.para: Once sgit existed, the vault rendered Markdown, images, CSV, audio, video and, by 30 March, HTML; Claude learnt to create vaults through skills. The 2 May brief set the sandbox model: the iframe cannot reach the network but can run JavaScript. By 8 May an app.json vault opened full screen as an app.

pace.line: Commits came daily, and agents wrote the code
pace.para: The app has 4,476 commits and 739 tags, peaking in March; the command line has 1,620 commits, two long pauses and an October burst, with tests rising from 237 to 4,232. Of my 1,671 app commits, 1,298 merge agent branches. Agents' share rose from 38% to over 85%.

market.line: The technology worked; the use case had not arrived
market.para: On 5 March the briefs said users buy credits, test once and don't come back; an April experiment with £5 model credits and a June profitability push followed, then a turn to RiskMandate. Nobody returned for more. Now the newsroom, RiskMandate and vaults supply workflows that need exactly these features.

limits.line: Memory was wrong in places, and usage was uncounted
limits.para: My memory was wrong on the order, the length of the Git work and the duration: eight months, not nine. Usage is described, not counted, and "30 paying customers" appears only in an investor one-pager, while ten is recorded. The iframe inspiration is recollection, and commit counts include CI automation.

sources.line: Sources: my memo, SG/Send and sgit repositories
sources.para: Based on my voice memo of 15 October 2026 and two research agents' reading of briefs, debriefs and commits in SGraph-AI__App__Send, SGit-AI__CLI and SG_Send__CLI, plus the sgit-ai releases on PyPI. Every date and quote was checked; counts come from git logs of all branches on 15 October 2026.
